newsitem.title: USA: U.N. fails to agree resolution on Iraq crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.N. fails to agree resolution on Iraq crisis.

text.p: United States ambassador to the United Nations, Madeleine Albright, said on Friday that the U.N. Security Council could not reach agreement on a resolution on the Iraqi crisis.

"The British said that while their text (of a draft Security Council resolution condemning Iraq for its incursion into protected Kurdish zones of the country last week) remains on the table that they have ceased conslut on it," said Albright after attending a Friday morning session of the Security Council.
Though not referred to by Alrbight, Russia's U.N. envoy said on Thursday that his country could not support the British text.
Iraqi President Saddam Hussein last weekend sent in his troops into internationally-protected Kurdish areas in support of one of the feuding faction there.

Washington retaliated this week with a series of missile attacks on air defense installations but recieved a mixed response from the former Gulf War coalition partners, with Russia declaring its opposition to the action.

The British draft text, which was the subject of deliberations over the previous two days, called for other countries to refrain from interfering in the internal Kurdish faction fighting and for the warring Kurd groups to resume talks.

Britain's deputy ambassador, Stepehn Gomersall, said after Friday's session that his country regretted that the council was not able to agree a resolution condemning Iraq's actions, despite a clear majority in favor.
The council can adopt a resolution if nine of the 15 countries vote in favor as long as none of the permanent five members -- the U.S., U.K., Russia, France and China -- votes against.

Russia's U.N. ambassador, Sergey Lavrov, said: "It was wise to agree not to proceed with any formal paper, especially because the situation has evolved in nrothern Iraq. There is no need to call upon anybody or demand from anybody to withdraw troops or do anything else."

U.S. ambassador Albright said: "We stand by what the United States did to deal with the problem in the northern governates and it is just unfortunate that at this stage the council was unable to speak on the subject."
Albright added: "It just shows that sometimes the council is not the most effective way to deal with this and the U.S. has sent the strongest signal."
